name: feverline-cpu-game
note: the self-playing cart: a team of four Normal CPUs on the Normal setup, every action entered by pressing the pad's actions toward the highlighted city or action; a full game ends with a result (the cart then plays match after match: done_once says one ended) (cured or lost) inside the frame budget, and both GPU hosts reach the same state hash. Control: the run one frame short differs. Frames within 1.2% of pixels: the glowing cubes, halos and bloom differ a little between GL and WebGPU

name: feverline-idle-seat
note: a CPU agent (Normal) first and a person who never touches the pad (the how-to-play card still open): the CPU takes its four actions under the card, the cards are drawn and the fever spreads, and the game waits for the person's agent. Control: the person's agent goes first instead, and nothing is played (0 decisions). Frames within 1.2% of pixels: the glowing cubes, halos and bloom differ a little between GL and WebGPU

name: feverline-newcomer
note: a newcomer alone on one pad, using only what the screen offers: the confirm press the setup card, the how-to-play card and every prompt name, every 20 frames. It begins on the setup card's highlighted choice (Intro, two agents), closes the how-to card, then takes the highlighted city or action each time (the cursor starts on the planner's suggestion) and the highlighted card when a hand is over the limit; a full game ends inside the budget (every move legal by construction: only legal targets are offered). Control: the same presses on the back action, which no prompt offers on the setup card, so the game never begins. Frames within 1.2% of pixels: the glowing cubes, halos and bloom differ a little between GL and WebGPU
